name: Milestone Delivery Progress
purpose: Measure how much engineering work for the current milestone has actually moved through feature design, implementation, automated verification, defect/review correction, regression re-test and product integration. MDP is a delivery-maturity tracker, not acceptance evidence and not a forecast.

milestoneBindingRules.featureDenominator: The active milestone must have an explicit finite feature/capability map whose weights sum to 100.
milestoneBindingRules.currentBinding: For SSJR-1.1, reuse the exact 20 frozen capability IDs and their exact SSJR weights. MDP does not alter SSJR scope, dependencies, weights, evidence layers or credit policy.
milestoneBindingRules.futureMilestones: When the owner selects a later milestone, bind MDP-1 to that milestone's explicit feature map. If no authoritative weighted feature map exists, define and review one before reporting an MDP score.

lifecycleStages.label: Design and contract
lifecycleStages.completionRule: The feature outcome, authority boundary, dependencies, supported states and material failure behavior are explicitly defined.

lifecycleStages.label: Implementation
lifecycleStages.completionRule: The milestone-specific end-to-end feature behavior is built. Reusable predecessor infrastructure by itself does not complete this stage.

lifecycleStages.label: Primary automated verification
lifecycleStages.completionRule: Deterministic automated coverage exercises the implemented feature's required success, denial and state-transition behavior at the relevant layers.

lifecycleStages.label: Defect and review resolution
lifecycleStages.completionRule: Known qualifying implementation defects and objective review findings for the feature are corrected. If none are found, a completed review/test triage may close this stage; never manufacture a bug for credit.

lifecycleStages.label: Regression re-test
lifecycleStages.completionRule: The corrected/reviewed feature is re-tested and its required regression gates pass on one coherent candidate head.

lifecycleStages.label: Product integration
lifecycleStages.completionRule: The feature is part of the authoritative product after the preceding lifecycle stages pass; runtime features must be merged and deployed/proven as the coherent product shell when deployment applies.

scoringRules.featureLifecyclePercent: Sum the lifecycle-stage weights whose state is complete. In-progress stages earn zero until their exit rule is satisfied.
scoringRules.milestoneScore: Sum all feature contributions and round to two decimal places.
scoringRules.reusableFoundationCredit: Do not mark a milestone-specific implementation stage complete merely because a reusable local, RJR, provider or reconciliation foundation exists. Count it only when wired into the specific milestone feature end to end.

separationFromReadiness.typicalRelationship: MDP will often be numerically above evidence-gated readiness because engineering can be complete before physical/production acceptance, but no invariant requires MDP to remain above SSJR.
separationFromReadiness.example: A feature may reach 100% MDP lifecycle maturity while remaining zero-credit in SSJR until every fixed SSJR evidence layer is accepted.

reporting.label: Milestone Delivery Progress
reporting.replaces: Estimated focused sessions to genuine SSJR100
reporting.updateRule: Recalculate whenever a current-milestone feature enters or completes a lifecycle stage, a qualifying regression invalidates a stage, or product integration changes.
